questions: Have you ever lost awareness or been unable to respond during these episodes?
Did the movements begin suddenly, over minutes or hours?
Do the movements completely stop when you are asleep?
Can you voluntarily suppress the movements for at least 30 seconds?
Do the movements lessen when you are distracted?
Do they become worse when someone watches or asks you to perform them?
Do you feel an urge or buildup immediately before a movement?
Does making the movement relieve that urge?
Are the movements identical each time they occur?
Do the movements change markedly in type, speed, or body part from one episode to another?
Do episodes occur with completely normal periods between them?
Are the movements worse during stress, anxiety, or emotional upset?
Did they begin after a physical injury, infection, medical procedure, or major emotional event?
Have you had similar movements or episodes in the past?
Have you taken an antipsychotic, anti-nausea medicine, antidepressant, stimulant, or other dopamine-affecting medicine?
Have you used cocaine, amphetamines, or other recreational stimulants?
Do you have weakness, numbness, difficulty speaking, or difficulty swallowing?
Have you had problems with balance, walking, vision, or coordination?
Have you had fever, severe headache, or neck stiffness with these movements?
Does anyone in your family have involuntary movements, seizures, or a progressive neurological disorder?
Have the movements gradually spread or worsened over weeks or months?
Do you make involuntary sounds, blink repeatedly, or have other repetitive habits?
Have you ever had a seizure diagnosed by a doctor?
Have you recently been pregnant, given birth, or had a major hormonal change?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a psychiatric or functional neurological disorder?
